subject: Request: first-frame parity + hybrid-fallback exception for mid-tier streaming plan
messages:
From: Olivia Chen <olivia.chen@quantahealth.com>
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, aditya_rao@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@quantahealth.com
Date: 2028-01-05T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: First-frame parity ask for hybrid streaming/batch workload

Hi Rishi / Aditya,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the model latency and cost profile look promising. One thing that came up with our engineering team: our front-end experiences expect identical "first-frame" behavior for both streaming and non-streaming endpoints so client-side rendering doesn't have to special-case two code paths.

Specifically Quanta Health is asking whether Redwood can offer an exception so that the mid-tier plan we're discussing guarantees near-parity on Time-To-First-Token (TTFT) between streaming endpoints and the equivalent non-streaming (sync) endpoints under normal load. If parity isn't feasible, we'd like a documented fallback: when streaming capacity is constrained, requests should fail over to a hybrid-sync path that still meets a firm TTFT of ~300ms and maintains a minimum tokens/sec of 80 for the first 4s of generation.

We understand this is atypical and may require routing or dedicated short bursts. Can you outline feasibility, measurable SLOs, how we'd see metrics in Console, and any commercial/credit implications? I've attached a short spreadsheet with our traffic profile.

Thanks,
Olivia Chen
Head of Integrations, Quanta Health
olivia.chen@quantahealth.com
(415) 555-0198

Attachment: qhealth-macscalc.xlsx

From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
To: Olivia Chen <olivia.chen@quantahealth.com>
Cc: aditya_rao@redwood.com, lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Date: 2028-01-05T12:37:00-08:00
Subject: Re: First-frame parity ask for hybrid streaming/batch workload

Hi Olivia — appreciate the clear ask and the traffic profile. Looping in Aditya (runtime infra) and Lauren (SA/Commercial) to scope the safe exception.

TL;DR: We can prototype an exception that provides the behavior you describe with three guardrails:
- Measured TTFT parity window: for up to 10k requests/day we can route a percentage of mid-tier streaming traffic to low-latency routing that preserves TTFT within +/-100ms of sync endpoints.
- Hybrid fallback: when low-latency pool is saturated, requests will fail over to a hybrid sync path with a guaranteed TTFT <= 300ms for the first token and a guaranteed emission floor of 80 tokens/sec for the first 4s (measured at token boundaries).
- Observability & billing: we'll expose token-level TTFT and first-4s token-rate metrics in Console under the "exceptions" namespace and apply a monthly exception fee or usage credit offset depending on the committed volume.

Questions for you so we can draft the formal carveout:
1) What % of traffic must be covered as parity (ex: 100% vs sampled 10-20%)?
2) Are the 80 tokens/sec and 4s floor hard requirements or a target we can phase in?
3) Any procurement constraints on monthly exception fees vs one-time ramp credits?

I've attached a quick comparison CSV (redwood-ttft-comparison.csv) showing how we measure TTFT across streaming vs sync in our benchmarks so you can validate measurement methodology. Aditya — can you confirm feasibility and list any infra changes (ephemeral routing, dedicated burst slots, or KV/cache tuning) we would need to enable this?

Thanks,
Rishi Malhotra
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.com

Attachment: redwood-ttft-comparison.csv

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, Olivia Chen <olivia.chen@quantahealth.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.com, jordan_blake@redwood.com
Date: 2028-01-06T08:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: First-frame parity ask for hybrid streaming/batch workload

Hi all,

Quick infra take from runtime: the parity guarantee is implementable as a combination of (A) short-lived priority routing into a low-latency pool, and (B) a hybrid sync fallback path if the low-latency pool is saturated. Implementation notes:
- Priority routing: add a routing tag on the request that attempts placement into a reserved low-latency slice. That slice can be sized to cover the first ~10k parity requests/day or expanded for a commitment.
- Fallback semantics: when the low-latency slice is full, we proxy to the hybrid sync worker which has a warmed KV/cache state and uses smaller batch windows to hit TTFT <= 300ms in 95th pct. To meet your 80 tokens/sec floor for the first 4s we can rate-prioritize the initial micro-batches; this costs extra GPU time.
- Telemetry & SLA: we will emit two new metrics: parity_ttft_95 and initial_tokens_per_second_4s_95. These will be visible in Console; we can also wire an alpha webhook into Quanta's telemetry pipeline for live alerts.

Operational considerations & commercial ask: to avoid noisy neighbor effects we recommend a small monthly exception fee (or a committed-burst add-on) for sustained parity coverage. If Quanta wants 100% parity coverage at scale we'll need a dedicated capacity pool (redwood dedicated) instead of a routed exception.

I'll draft a short exception document and hand it to Legal/Commercial for review.

—Aditya
Lead Runtime Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Olivia Chen <olivia.chen@quantahealth.com>
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, aditya_rao@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@quantahealth.com, lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Date: 2028-01-07T15:34:00-08:00
Subject: Re: First-frame parity ask for hybrid streaming/batch workload

Thanks Rishi/Aditya — that plan is helpful and captures what we need. A few quick items before we proceed:

1) Coverage: we'd like parity for 50% of request volume during business hours (PT 8am–6pm) and sampled parity outside that window. If there's an easy toggle to expand to 100% with a committed burst add-on, include pricing.
2) Measurement: the metrics and 95th pct sounds right. We need the Console dashboards and a weekly CSV export for the pilot.
3) Procurement: Quanta prefers a one-time ramp credit + monthly exception fee rather than an ongoing usage surcharge. We'll route formal terms through procurement but want a redline-ready exception draft.

Next step: can you send the exception draft and a DocuSign-ready statement of work? If it's okay, procurement will aim to sign within two weeks once commercial terms are in the draft.

Appreciate the fast turn.
Olivia

Attachment: none

From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
To: Olivia Chen <olivia.chen@quantahealth.com>
Cc: aditya_rao@redwood.com, lauren_bishop@redwood.com, jordan_blake@redwood.com
Date: 2028-01-07T16:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: First-frame parity ask for hybrid streaming/batch workload

Olivia — noted. We'll:
- Draft an exception that sets parity coverage at 50% business-hours with a toggle for 100% via committed-burst add-on.
- Include visibility requirements: parity_ttft_95 and initial_tokens_per_second_4s_95 in Console + weekly CSV export.
- Offer commercial structure: one-time ramp credit + monthly exception fee; we will include sample numbers in the draft.

I'll upload the exception draft and DocuSign link by tomorrow EOD. Jordan will help with the contract flow.

Best,
Rishi
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference
